title: Nesting one level past maxDepth stringifies the subtree instead of expanding it
rationale: The cliff edge from above, and the fixture that documents what the truncation actually is. Most readers assume exceeding maxDepth drops or throws; it does neither - the whole subtree is replaced by its JSON text under the parent key, at log.debug only.
catchesBugClass: A change in truncation STRATEGY - silently switching to dropping the subtree, to a placeholder token, or to partial expansion. Any of those would be a wire-format change for every over-deep document.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the ambiguity it creates; that requires the paired fixture. It also cannot catch the asymmetry with lists, and says nothing about whether ACCEPTED is the right verdict.

predicted.detail: Bounding depth necessarily truncates, and embedding the exact JSON text is the least-destructive truncation available: every byte survives. What is not defensible is that the type change carries no marker.

configDescription: MapFlattener.builder().maxDepth(3); flat map must equal depth-overflow-aliases-a-real-string
